extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH grant applications and mentored career-development award applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing the Rigor and Reproducibility components of NIH grant and career-development applications, describing required elements, field-specific expectations, and reviewer considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Rigor Is Scored
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific rigor contributes to the Approach criterion for research project grant applications, to the Research Plan criterion for mentored career development award applications, and to the overall impact score. In the Simplified Peer Review Framework (2025+), rigor is part of Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that reviewers will evaluate rigor within these formal scoring criteria; describe rigor elements so they map clearly to Approach/Research Plan and to Factor 2 considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of the Prior Research (Significance/Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths and weaknesses of the published research and/or preliminary data; critical evaluation of prior work, not just description; support for proposed research; where science is contested or unsettled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers ask: "Is the scientific premise sound?" Provide critical analysis of existing literature and preliminary data to justify the proposed work and explicitly acknowledge limitations or uncertainty in prior studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Rigor (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The strict application of the scientific method: robust experimental design; adequate statistical power; sample size justification; pre-specified analysis plan; methods to minimize bias (blinding, randomization); inclusion of appropriate controls; plans for testing reproducibility; independent validation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers ask: "Is the design rigorous?" Explicitly describe design choices (power/sample-size calculations, analysis plans, randomization/blinding procedures, control selection), reproducibility testing, and any independent validation or replication strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Relevant Biological Variables (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address relevant biological variables such as sex as a biological variable (SABV) — required since 2016 — age, race/ethnicity when relevant to the scientific question, weight/body composition as appropriate, genetic background in animal models; provide justification if studying a single sex or limited demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers ask: "Are biological variables addressed?" Explicitly state how biological variables will be considered, measured, and analyzed, and justify any limitations in scope (e.g., single-sex studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (Authentication Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication plan submitted as a separate attachment covering cell lines (verify identity, mycoplasma testing), antibodies (validation methods), other key biological resources (e.g., transgenic animals), and custom-made or sourced-from-nonvalidated suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers ask: "Are resources authenticated?" Provide concrete authentication and validation methods (e.g., STR profiling for cell lines, mycoplasma testing, antibody validation) and mention frequency/timing of checks and provenance of critical reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Studies Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For animal studies: number of animals justified by power calculation; both sexes used unless justification provided; randomization to experimental groups; blinded outcome assessment; pre-registered analysis where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe power/sample-size calculations, sex-inclusion plans or justification for exclusion, randomization and blinding procedures, and whether/when analyses will be pre-registered; align with ARRIVE and other animal-research standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell Culture Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For cell-culture work: cell line authentication (STR profiling); mycoplasma testing; multiple independent biological replicates; use of multiple cell lines where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on how cell lines will be authenticated and tested, the number/type of biological replicates, and rationale for the number/types of cell lines used to support generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Studies Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For human studies: power calculation; recruitment plan to enroll diverse population; plan for handling missing data; blinding where feasible; pre-specified outcomes; statistical analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include recruitment strategies to achieve diversity, concrete missing-data handling and analytic approaches, and pre-specify outcomes and statistical methods to reduce bias and increase reproducibility; reference CONSORT when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Approach Pitfalls Related to Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pitfalls that undermine rigor include inadequate sample size justification; single-replicate experiments; cherry-picked data; underpowered studies; lack of negative/positive controls; no randomization mentioned; no blinding of analyses; no mention of how variability will be handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these anti-patterns by providing transparent, quantitative justifications for design choices, including controls, replication, randomization/blinding, and explicit plans for handling variability and selection of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Resources to Support Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources NIH provides include Rigor and Reproducibility Training Modules, iCite (citation analysis), sample size and power calculators, ARRIVE Guidelines for animal research, and CONSORT for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these NIH-provided tools and established reporting guidelines to strengthen and document the rigor and reproducibility elements of the application.
